headline_findings: COACH-ANSWER ATH-01 / CAT-10: what decides plyos vs ballistics is how long the sport keeps the athlete on the ground - short contacts (sprinters) -> more plyos, long contacts (karate, fighters, baseball) -> more ballistics, basketball 'a good mix'; programs start ballistic and become plyometric. v1 encodes a `ground_contact` class (1-5) per sport and derives the plyo share of power sets (PROPOSED map 75 / 60 / 50 / 40 / 25%, floor 20, ceiling 80). OBSERVED anchors from a re-count of his own programs by ground contact: BASEBALL blocks 44% / 36% / 44% plyo side, BOXER weeks 3-6 30%, MM athletic STARTING / MID / ADVANCED 33% / 8% / 9% (throw-dominant).

COACH-ANSWER ATH-02 (ranking confirmed): basketball = volleyball > sprinters > football skill > soccer > MMA > tennis > baseball > hockey > wrestling / BJJ > boxing = karate > golf. v1 applies it to FAST-reactive plyometric contacts (the ground-contact definition): the boxer's 113-129 weekly jump contacts are mostly ballistic jumps (66) and landings (24), only 31 are fast-reactive, below baseball's 37 / 58 / 74 - so the coach's own programs agree with his ranking once contacts are classified his way. Targets follow the ranking by construction (section 5.12).

COACH-ANSWER UNI-02 / UNI-03 / UNI-10: bilateral : unilateral runs from 90/10 to 10/90 by athlete, goal, phase and pain - bodybuilders / powerlifters about 50/50 at the start then 80/20-90/10 bilateral, field / change-of-direction athletes 80-90% unilateral, bilateral minimal in season; unilateral = health and rotational foundation, bilateral = driving force; upper body the same. OBSERVED today: 26-32% unilateral in strength / conjugate, ~50% in the BYOP 4-day templates, 43-47% in baseball (every block, including in-season), 50-75% in the MM athletic blocks, 63% HYBRID. v1 sets block-start / block-end / in-season values per profile (section 5.11).

COACH-ANSWER CAT-13 / UNI-12 / UNI-06: contralateral loading pulls you INTO the hip (change-of-direction athletes: football, soccer, basketball, tennis), ipsilateral helps you OUT of the hip (sprint acceleration - ipsilateral step-ups); for bodybuilders / powerlifters contra/ipsi work is a health accessory mostly in weeks 1-4. Court and combat athletes get more frontal / transverse unilateral work, aesthetics clients little. Same-pattern pairing (squat + lunge) drives a muscle harder (aesthetics, high-level athletes); cross-pattern pairing keeps bootcamp clients less sore.

ground_contact_model.evidence: COACH-ANSWER ATH-01 / CAT-10 (rule); class map PROPOSED - PENDING COACH APPROVAL
ground_contact_model.science: fast stretch-shortening cycle = ground contact under about 250 ms, slow SSC = over about 250 ms (Schmidtbleicher's split, used by Flanagan & Comyns 2008 to prescribe plyometrics by contact time and reactive strength index [S32]); sprint contacts average about 0.14-0.16 s in acceleration and shorten toward maximal velocity, and faster accelerators show shorter contacts [S33]

plyo_method_stages.name: plyo method stages (the coach has not named this yet - it is NOT a plyo zone, COACH-ANSWER CAT-11; 'zones' are Davidson rotation zones and do not apply to plyos, CAT-10)

stages.label: receive and pause
stages.examples: stick-the-landing drills, depth drops with a 3 s stick, 'Push up Stick the Landing' (hands start on a box and land on the floor, LIB-02)

stages.label: receive then create (one response)
stages.examples: stick the landing then jump / hop, depth drop to jump, drop into box jump

stages.label: repeated receive / create
stages.examples: repeated hops, hurdle hops (taller hurdles + continuous quick contacts = advanced, LIB-04), pogos, bounds

rules: the stage is a way of PERFORMING a jump ('more like the way I want the plyos to be done'), not a fixed property of the exercise: the same hurdle hop can be done stick-and-pause, single response or repeated - COACH-ANSWER CAT-11
programs START more ballistic and gradually become more plyometric (connective-tissue tolerance and structure) - COACH-ANSWER CAT-10
unilateral plyos are harder than bilateral ones; progress bilateral -> unilateral inside each stage - COACH-ANSWER CAT-10

PROPOSED timing (pending): 12-week plan = weeks 1-3 stage 1 + ballistic-biased mix (plyo share -15 points, floor 20), weeks 4-7 stage 2, weeks 8-12 stage 3 at the sport's target share; 8-week plan = weeks 1-2 / 3-5 / 6-8; 4-6-week maintenance blocks stay at the current stage; L2-L3 athletes may start at stage 2

bilateral_unilateral_model.scale: share of lower-body compound sets that are BILATERAL : UNILATERAL, anywhere from 90/10 to 10/90 (COACH-ANSWER UNI-02); upper body follows the same logic for pressing and pulling (UNI-03); coach-adjustable
bilateral_unilateral_model.why: 'the unilateral work is more for health and keeping rotational foundations, and the bilateral is more for driving and creating forces' (UNI-02)
anchors: bodybuilders / powerlifters: about 50/50 at the start (unilateral as a small health foundation), then 80/20 -> 90/10 bilateral (COACH-ANSWER UNI-02)
field / change-of-direction athletes (tennis example): 80-90% unilateral in the gym; bilateral = health foundation for connective tissue and joints (COACH-ANSWER UNI-02)
in-season athletes: bilateral kept minimal (maintain strength and potentiation), unilateral keeps ranges of motion and health (COACH-ANSWER UNI-10)
pain or injury moves the share (usually toward unilateral / split grips, or to machines) - COACH-ANSWER UNI-02, VOL-03, MASTER_MODEL athletic A6
bilateral_unilateral_model.engine: share(week) = start + (end - start) x week_fraction across the off-season block (the coach's set-addition order adds sets to the FIRST exercise first, VOL-07, and bilateral slots come first, so the bilateral share rises naturally for size/strength goals); in-season value replaces it during the season; pain overrides; the weekly-set baseline in section 5.2 uses the mid-block value (PROPOSED). For profiles whose share moves TOWARD unilateral (field / COD athletes, e.g. basketball 20/80 -> 10/90), the share target decides where an added set goes: when adding it to the first (bilateral) exercise would move the share away from the week's target, it goes to the first unilateral exercise instead (PROPOSED - reconciles VOL-07 with UNI-02).

contra_ipsi.contralateral: load in the hand opposite the working leg pulls you INTO the hip (eccentric coil); used for change-of-direction athletes who must get in and out of the hip quickly and need the range (football route runners, soccer, basketball 'a lot', tennis 'definitely') - COACH-ANSWER CAT-13

assembly_rules: 1. Intake (COACH-ANSWER GEN-02): goal; competitive sport -> sport + position + season, recreational -> general sport only (weekend-warrior profile); training experience in YEARS (-> L1 / L2 / L3, PRG-05); age; body weight; days; session length; equipment; injuries / pain; priority muscles; rep-style preference; plan type. NO sex field (GEN-02, ATH-09).

2. Pick the profile (+ position variant), season phase and competition level (high school / college / pro = same plan, different loads - PRG-09). A competitive sport without a profile uses the nearest profile by ground-contact class and ATH-03 group (PROPOSED).

3. Weekly set budget per category = profile.weekly_sets (v1 off-season build baseline) x season multiplier x the volume engine's person-based weekly rate (3 / 5 / 7% of weekly sets chosen by fatigue, life and response, never 10%/week - VOL-04 / VOL-05 / UNI-05; see 03 v1 / 12_volume_algorithm_v1). Plan type shapes the curve (PER-01): 4-6-week maintenance at 50-70% volume, 8-week = 4 adapt + 4 drive, 12-week = 2-4 acclimation + 4-6 build + hardest last weeks.

4. Power block: split power sets plyo : ballistic by the ground-contact class (ATH-01; map PROPOSED), start ballistic-biased and move to the target (CAT-10); plyo method stage 1 -> 2 -> 3 across the block; unilateral plyos after bilateral; medball volume by sport, none for aesthetics, ball <= 20 lb (ATH-05 / EQ-06); Olympic lifts for every athletic trainee at their level (ATH-10); contrast only L2+ off-season (ATH-12).

5.
